title: Kung Pao Chicken
subtitle: Spiced chicken with peanuts and dried chilli
excerpt: Chicken breast stir-fried with dried red chilli, roasted peanuts, garlic and ginger in a sharp, slightly sweet sauce. The hallmarks of this Sichuan dish are the numbing heat from the dried chillies and the textural contrast of the crunchy peanuts. The sauce thickens in seconds once the cornflour slurry goes in, so have everything prepped before the wok goes on the heat.
sourceNotes: Kung pao chicken is a Sichuan dish attributed to Ding Baozhen, a Qing dynasty official whose posthumous title was 'Gong Bao'; the dish was suppressed as 'feudal' during the Cultural Revolution before being rehabilitated and spreading globally.

content.text: Note on gluten-free: soy sauce contains wheat unless specifically labelled tamari or gluten-free soy sauce. Use tamari in place of the light soy sauce here if you need the dish to be strictly gluten-free. The dish is listed as glutenFree on the basis that tamari works as a direct swap. A wok on very high heat is the right tool: the high sides and wide base let you toss the ingredients quickly without them spilling, and the intense heat is essential for proper stir-frying.

items.prepNote: dried, halved; or 2 fresh chillies, sliced
mixed with 2 tbsp cold water to form a slurry

content.text: Mix the soy sauce (or tamari), rice vinegar, honey and cornflour slurry together in a small bowl. Set the sauce mixture aside.

Heat the wok over the highest heat until smoking. Add the sunflower oil, then add the dried chillies. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until they darken slightly. Add the chicken cubes and spread them across the wok. Leave undisturbed for 90 seconds to colour, then toss and cook for another 2 minutes until cooked through. Remove to a plate.
Add the garlic, ginger and red pepper to the wok. Stir-fry for 2 minutes. Return the chicken to the wok. Add the spring onions and toss briefly.

Pour in the sauce mixture. Toss everything together; the sauce will thicken within 30 to 60 seconds as the cornflour heats. Add the peanuts and drizzle with sesame oil. Serve immediately over steamed rice.

items.symptom: Sauce is too thick and pasty
items.cause: Too much cornflour or the slurry was too concentrated
items.fix: Add 2 to 3 tablespoons of water and toss over the heat until loosened to a glossy coating consistency.

items.cause: Cut too large or cooked at too low a temperature for the volume
items.fix: Keep pieces to 2cm and make sure the wok is fully smoking before the chicken goes in. Cook in two batches if the wok is not large enough.
